title.narrative: Nevado del Ruiz Volcano Emergency Response

description.narrative: Since March 24, 2023, there has been a significant increase in seismic activity of the Nevado del Ruiz volcano in Colombia. As of March 30, the Colombian Geological Service (SGC) changed the alert level from yellow to orange, which indicates that there is a probability that in days or weeks there will be an eruption larger than any seen in the previous 10 years. The national government indicates that the alert level may go to red in the next few days, due to the continued seismic activity. Likewise, a hospital red alert was declared in order to be prepared for a possible catastrophe. The area of influence includes 22 municipalities in the departments of Tolima, Caldas, Risaralda, Valle del Cauca, Quindío and Cundinamarca, where more than 57,000 people live. A diagnosis carried out by the SNPS- CC identified that the ash fall and the expulsion of toxic gases have generated the contamination of water sources, that the population does not have emergency kits, and that much of the population does not have sufficient information and is unaware of safe evacuation routes. This project will target 370 families out of the most vulnerable households in two municipalities in Caldas department. Hygiene training will be carried out to mitigate the risk of disease from contaminated water, alongside first aid kit distributions. Water filtration systems will also be distributed to provide a source of uncontaminated water. Emergency kits will be provided to families, containing NFIs essential in case of an eruption. These deliveries will be accompanied by a communication strategy through local media, and workshops to raise awareness of the population with safe evacuation routes and alerts from the Colombian Geological Service, in order to make the population aware of the risks to which they are exposed.
